item.text: {"search_note":"I found strong evidence for surveillance, censorship, and harassment. I did not find a credible Egypt-specific 2024 report showing a nationwide internet blackout or a major deliberate shutdown campaign in Egypt itself. One relevant 2024 effect was broader power cuts affecting access, but that is not the same as an intentional internet shutdown.","evidence":[{"title":"Sandvine was used to enable mass web monitoring and censorship in Egypt","publisher":"Access Now","date":"2024-02-27","url":"https://www.accessnow.org/press-release/us-blocklists-sandvine-for-digital-repression-in-egypt/","summary":"The U.S. Entity List action was prompted by Sandvine’s sale of deep packet inspection technology to Egypt, which Access Now says facilitated mass web-monitoring, censorship, and targeting of activists and politicians.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6"]},{"title":"Internet freedom remained severely constrained by surveillance and harassment","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-net/2024","summary":"Freedom House says criminal penalties, harassment, and surveillance fueled self-censorship among Egyptian internet users. It also notes website blocking and repression of critics, which directly fits digital control.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6","4B.5"]},{"title":"Independent groups were kept under intrusive reporting and constant surveillance","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/location/middle-east-and-north-africa/egypt/report-egypt/","summary":"Amnesty says associations faced unlawful authorization rules, intrusive reporting requirements, and NSA intimidation, effectively placing them under constant surveillance and limiting their freedom of association.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.4","4B.5"]},{"title":"HRW documented digital targeting through arbitrary phone searches and online entrapment","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/egypt","summary":"HRW says LGBT people were entrapped online, extorted online, and prosecuted using illegitimately obtained digital information based on arbitrary phone searches. That is direct evidence of digital controls used to limit political and social freedom.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.7","4B.6","4B.5"]},{"title":"HRW reported severe restrictions, harassment, and asset freezes against rights groups and activists","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/egypt","summary":"HRW says NGOs faced judicial and security harassment, travel bans, asset freezes, and prosecution under restrictive laws. This is administrative harassment used to limit civic and political space.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.4","4B.5"]},{"title":"Security forces used social-media activity as a trigger for arrests","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-05-13","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/","summary":"Amnesty documented arrests of people criticizing price hikes online, questioning of striking workers, and dispersal of a protest. This shows online speech was monitored and punished as a form of political control.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6","4B.5"]},{"title":"Authorities made a new wave of arrests over online protest calls","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-07-18","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-more-than-100-arbitrarily-detained-over-calls-for-anti-government-protests/","summary":"Amnesty says 119 people were detained after social-media calls for protests, with charges tied to posts and online mobilization. That is strong evidence of digital surveillance plus administrative repression.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6","4B.5"]},{"title":"Journalists faced raids, device seizure, secret detention, and prosecution","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-08-29","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/29/egypt-spate-free-speech-prosecutions","summary":"HRW reports security forces raided a journalist’s home, seized electronic devices, and prosecutors held him in secret detention under broad security-style charges. This is direct administrative harassment and digital control against press freedom.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6","4B.5"]}]}
